manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pour all the water from the bowl on the left into the bowl on the right.

Task description: The light green bowl on the left contains water, and the light green bowl on the right is empty. Transfer the water from the left bowl into the right bowl without spilling onto the table.

Success criteria: Nearly all the water from the left bowl has entered the right bowl, with no spilled water on the table.

## Execution tips

- Consider grasping a section of the left bowl's rim near the front table edge, with one finger inside and one against the outer wall, leaving space on the pouring side toward the right bowl. Match the opening to local wall thickness plus finger clearance, placing the pads against the inner and outer walls below the rim to reduce slipping from a grasp on the thin edge alone.
- Before closing, use both views to confirm the fingers lie inside and outside the bowl wall, avoiding misleading gripper occlusion. Check for slipping with a small test lift, and restore bowl-bottom support on the table before regrasping.
- When carrying the bowl with water, keep it nearly level, avoid sudden stops and swinging, and leave clearance between its base and the right bowl's rim to avoid spilling water or knocking over the receiving bowl.
- During pouring, place the left bowl's pouring rim above the right bowl opening with margin from its edge and a small, collision-free drop. Increase tilt incrementally and adjust position according to the actual stream landing point to reduce overshoot and splashing.
- When the stream thins, pause to observe remaining left-bowl water and any flow down the outer wall, avoiding sudden flipping or shaking. While dripping continues, keep the drip point above the right opening.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this real-robot episode with your parameters and follow the returned manual and live observations; when finished or unable to continue, I will call finish_episode.

Live observations confirm water in the left bowl and an empty right bowl; only the right arm is currently available. Adjusting the gripper's downward angle reached a controller joint limit. I will adjust the approach position within this episode using the returned actual pose.
The gripper is near the outside rim of the left bowl. Next I will open it and lower in small steps to confirm the fingers are on the inner and outer sides of the wall, then close and test-lift.

The gripper has grasped the bowl rim with a measured opening of approximately 7–8 mm. The rim remained between the pads during a small test lift. I will continue lifting slowly and confirm bottom clearance before moving toward the right bowl.

During the continued test lift, the gripper opening narrowed and the bowl's pose changed, so I cannot yet confirm a stable grasp. I will lower the bowl to restore table support, then adjust the grasp angle and depth.

The bowl remains supported by the table and has not been moved or tipped. The new grasp angle has increased the closing gap noticeably. I will further adjust the pad angle relative to the bowl wall and check the grasp again.
The pads have been adjusted to better match the bowl-wall slope. Next I will close again and make a small test lift. The live view has not yet shown water spilling outside the bowl.

During this test lift, the gripper opening stayed at about 2.7 mm, and the bowl rose with the gripper; the grasp is steadier than before. I am increasing the height above the table to clear the rim of the right bowl.
The left bowl is off the table and remains securely held, moving in small steps above the right bowl. Once aligned, I will increase the tilt gradually and adjust based on where the water lands.

The left bowl has been tilted gradually above the opening of the right bowl. Water is gathering toward the pouring side, but a continuous stream is not visible yet. I will adjust slightly and check the gap between the bowls and the landing point of the water.

I observed a slight shift in the right bowl, and the gap between the bowls may be insufficient. I will pause increasing the tilt, lift slightly, and adjust the pose to restore clearance before deciding whether to continue.
I saw water flowing into the right bowl and landing inside it. The stream has weakened at the current tilt, so I will tilt slightly more to transfer the remaining water.

The right bowl has received some water, but visible water marks appeared on the table to its left, so I cannot currently judge that the condition of no water spilled on the table is met. Lateral movement again reached a joint limit. I will adjust based on the actual pose to direct subsequent flow and drips into the right bowl as far as possible.

The tool reported that authorization cannot cover the next action, and the episode entered a safety pause. I will immediately call finish_episode. The gripper still holds the tilted left bowl, requiring the on-site operator to take over; ending the logical episode does not guarantee that the arm has physically stopped or will maintain holding torque.
